H1.observation: Diagnostic distractor-agreement accuracy is 57/128; correct main-subject agreement often loses to a nearby plural distractor. Existing attention branches mix context, with layer-output norms 0.13–0.69.
H1.hypothesis: Change the gain of contextual attention relative to the residual stream throughout the existing blocks.
H1.formula: For all eight blocks, scale attention.out_proj.weight and out_proj.bias together.
H1.prediction: A stronger contextual branch may improve agreement decisions; a weaker counter-direction tests that interpretation. Observe all regressions.
H1.risk: All attention computations are rescaled, including useful ones. Stronger incorrect attention may worsen grammar and story generation.

H2.observation: Read-only diagnostic mean FFN output norm is 0.877 in block 0 and 0.222 in block 7; block-7 residual before FFN is 0.173. Many mistakes favour familiar lexical alternatives or distractor agreement.
H2.hypothesis: Rebalance FFN updates that can overwrite contextual evidence; reduced gain may preserve useful attention/residual information.
H2.formula: For all eight blocks, scale mlp.c_proj.weight and c_proj.bias together. Do not change activation, width, forward, embeddings or readout.
H2.prediction: Modest reduction can help contextual agreement, while an increase is an explicit counter-direction. Norms alone are not causal proof.
H2.risk: FFN updates are co-adapted to residual and attention paths. Even modest global rescaling can destroy useful cancellations or lexical knowledge.

H3.observation: Diagnostic agreement failures can involve competition between source tokens. This tests attention concentration separately from H1 output amplitude; it does not assume the correct token always ranks first.
H3.hypothesis: Change the concentration of existing attention distributions without replacing their learned directions.
H3.formula: For all eight blocks, scale attention.q_proj.weight. Query-key scores scale by the same factor; K, V and the causal/local mask remain fixed.
H3.prediction: Sharper or softer selection can alter agreement evidence where context sources compete; validation decides whether the predicted benefit exists.
H3.risk: Sharpening a wrong maximum reinforces it; softening can dilute a useful precise source.

combinations.rule: Choose best singleton in each family by the registered validation ranking; evaluate H1+H2, H1+H3, H1+H2+H3 with those exact coefficients. No new coefficient fitting.

degrees_of_freedom: Many scalar values change, but the search has only explicit group coefficients; this is not evidence of many independently designed computations.
forbidden_methods: No gradients, optimizer, regression, evolutionary method, random candidate search, training or output-temperature-only edit.
